newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen shares end sharply down on rumours.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen shares end sharply down on rumours.

text.p: Shenzhen's A and B share indices closed sharply lower on Monday on poor sentiment influenced by by rumours on the health of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, brokers said.
The A share index dived 21.18 points or 6.22 percent to end at 319.25 on turnover of 3.78 billion yuan compared with Friday's 5.92 billion yuan.
The B index tumbled 5.71 points or 4.02 percent to close at 136.46 on turnover of HK$89 million against HK$161 million.
"There have been many rumours in the market that Deng was in poor health," a broker said.

Brokers said the declines were also due to expectations among investors that many of China's listed firms were unlikely to report a significant rise in earnings for 1996 despite two interest rate cuts last year.
"The downword trend could extend into the next few sessions unless there is some good news," a second broker said.
All 43 Shenzhen-listed B shares traded, with 42 falling and one rising.
Lizhu Pharmaceutical was the worst performer on the B share market, diving HK$0.32, or 7.19 percent, to HK$4.13 on volume of 407,500 shares.
Chiwan Petroleum followed with a drop of HK$0.30 or 6.98 percent to HK$4.00, with 167,600 shares traded.
Changan Automobile was the most active stock on volume of 2.95 million shares and slipped HK$0.18 to HK$4.27.
Washing machine maker Little Swan bucked the trend with a rise of HK$0.02 to HK$7.90 on trade of 265,800 shares.
On the A share market, selling focused on cheap-priced stocks, brokers said.
Hainan Pearl River slid 0.62 yuan to end a limit-down of 5.54 yuan due to pessimism over the property developer's 1996 results, brokers said.
